elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Subparagraph 18.1A expressly permits the Customer to terminate “this Agreement or its participation in this Agreement for convenience.”

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Termination is permitted upon 30 days’ prior written notice.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: The other Parties must refund, pro rata, amounts prepaid for the period after the termination effective date.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: During the 25-year Initial Period, termination otherwise requires written agreement of all Parties; the unilateral right of any other Party arises only at the end of the Initial Period or thereafter.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The operative notice requirement is 30 days, not a requirement of 60 to 90 days.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee applies to termination under Subparagraph 18.1A. The no-credit provision applies only to termination under Subparagraph 18.1, so the conditional cap is satisfied by the absence of such a fee.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Subparagraph 18.1 permits any Party to terminate at the end of the Initial Period “or any time thereafter,” rather than only at the end of a term.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Any Party exercising the Subparagraph 18.1 right must provide at least one year’s prior written notice, exceeding 90 days.
